answer:
K-means minimizes squared distances to centroids, favoring roughly spherical similarly scaled clusters. GMMs assign soft memberships to Gaussian components and can represent elliptical clusters. DBSCAN groups density-connected points and marks sparse points as noise, handling nonconvex rings but struggling when densities differ under one global radius. Agglomerative clustering repeatedly merges groups according to a chosen linkage. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html)

$$J_{kmeans}=\sum_i\|x_i-\mu_{c_i}\|^2.$$

Single linkage can follow nonconvex shapes but suffers chaining; complete/Ward linkage favors different geometry. Neither cluster count nor a visually attractive plot proves meaningful structure. Choose distance, scaling, noise policy, and hyperparameters based on the task, then assess stability and domain usefulness. GMM component count need not equal the number of semantic classes.
